text:
Sam W: FYI incoming from ACME deal room — they want a one-week POC but insist on region-bound processing and a signed SLA exception for <50ms tail latency in EU. asking for routing/subproc whitelist + kms availability.
Dana R: ack. can you paste the exact enterprise asks from legal?
Sam W: copied below from their SecReqs doc: "data must not leave EU, sub-processors must be disclosed and approved, kms keys in customer-managed HSM, routes pinned to eu-west or eu-central, fallback only to other EU regions, and SLA clause for latency with financial penalties."
Chris L: couple quick notes: 1) hosted API currently routes to nearest healthy region by default, 2) we can support tenant pinning to eu-* (dedicated or private preferred), 3) KMS in customer HSM is only available on Private deployments.
Olivia P: for a one-week POC the simplest path is Redwood Dedicated in eu-west + tenant pin. that avoids cross-region egress and satisfies the residence ask. costwise thats a small reserved commit or a short-term dedicated trial.
Maya S: security checklist: we need the customer to sign our subprocessor list and a DPA addendum. also need proof of their HSM provider if they require key import/export procedures.
Sam W: can we do a temporary flow where the request headers include a routing policy and we set a policy override for this tenant for the POC?
Chris L: yes — we can create a per-tenant routing policy. sample policy: ```
route_policy:
  regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
  preferred: eu-west-1
  failover: eu-central-1
  allow_fallback_outside_eu: false
```
Sam W: perfect. what about subprocessor disclosure — they want a whitelist before POC starts.
Maya S: share our current subproc list link: https://redwood.internal/security/subprocessors (internal). we'll need their legal to confirm within 48h for an expedited POC.
Dana R: pricing Q: if we pin to dedicated eu-west1 for a week, approximate uplift vs hosted?
Olivia P: rough ballpark: 2-3x hosted token rate due to reserved GPU cost, but we can offer a short-term discounted trial rate for Sales closes under 30d. I'll draft pricing options.
Sam W: ops question: who owns the routing policy change and the SLA exception doc?
Chris L: Eng owns the routing policy implementation, Security + Legal own the SLA exception template. I can provision the policy and put it behind a canary flag for 7d.
eng-ops-bot: new routing-policy request created: rp-1755555555; assignee: Chris L.
Maya S: I'll start the subprocessor clearance and DPA addendum. need the customer's legal contact + HSM provider details.
Dana R: I'll coordinate the pricing note and get the discount approved. Sam, can you ask ACME for the legal contact and HSM vendor by EOD?
Sam W: on it. pinging ACME legal: @acme-legal can you share the HSM provider and confirm you'll sign the DPA addendum within 48h?
Olivia P: for the POC SLOs: if they insist on <50ms tail, we should clarify measurement method (p95/p99, ingress location). call that out in the exception.
Sam W: noted — will clarify p99 tail and measurement from eu-west egress.
Chris L: one more ops note: KV cache and batching may change tail latency. we'll set conservative batching for the POC and monitor.
Sam W: awesome. next steps: 1) ACME legal to confirm HSM + sign DPA addendum, 2) Sales to agree pricing option, 3) Eng to provision tenant routing policy and dedicated pool, 4) Security to clear subprocessors. target POC start: next Tue if everything green. :rocket:
Dana R: great — I'll update the deal room and add links to the required docs.
Maya S: adding checklist items to the thread: subproc clearance, HSM proof, signed DPA, SLA exception template approved.
Sam W: thanks all. I'll follow up after ACME replies.
